Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and headache. The reported
mechanism of injury is cnosistent with the severity of the impact, and the presenting symptoms align with a cervical strain
pattern. Over the course of care, the patient attended 25 visits, which is somewhat longer than typically expected for this type of
injury, and progress was gradual. Range of motion testing and palpation revealed findings that support the clinical diagnosis,
including reduced cervical rotation and localized paraspinal tenderness, while several neurological screening tests and
imaging-related assessments returned within normal limits. No prior injury or treatment to the cervical spine is known from the
patient history. Billing records were reviewed and show no duplicate or repeated charges for services rendered. Ongiong home
exercise instruction was provided, and the patient was advised to return if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs develop.
